HTML

This page is a stub. It starts a minimal introduction to HTML. The first step is written below. The later steps are an outline. The introduction ends with two places to continue.

The first step

HTML is the markup a browser reads as a page. The first orientation is this: the page is a document, and the tags around the words tell the browser what each part is. A tag is a name written between angle brackets.

The rest of this mini introduction

These steps are the intended outline. They are not written out as lessons yet.

  1. A tag names one part of the document, such as a heading or a paragraph.
  2. A link is a tag that points at another page.
  3. The words a person reads, and the tags around them, are both in the file.
  4. A full document has a head and a body. These course lessons are the body piece.
